locations.name: Vermont
locations.subtitle: Stowe / Killington / Mad River Valley

weather.notes: Foliage past-peak up north, still vibrant in central/southern VT

nyc.note: Year-round, no seasonal cutoff — Delta (JFK/LGA), United (EWR) and American (JFK). About 1h30.

sf.note: No Bay Area nonstop to BTV in any season. One stop via a hub; ~9h door to door.

seattle.note: No nonstop, ever. One stop, and the longest travel day of anything on this list.

locations.verdict: Best classic-foliage trip, but priciest flights for SF/Seattle crew

locations.name: Wyoming
locations.subtitle: Jackson Hole / Grand Teton

weather.precip: ~13 days w/ snow, up to 30cm possible
weather.notes: Coldest option, chance of a snow squall

nyc.note: American's JFK nonstop last flies Oct 4. United's Newark nonstop does run to Oct 24 — but Saturdays and Sundays only from Sept 25, so it can't do a Friday out and a Monday back. On your dates: connect via Denver or Salt Lake.

sf.note: United flies SFO–JAC daily Sept 24 through Oct 24, so your dates sit inside the window with five days to spare. Alaska's SFO nonstop ended Aug 18.

seattle.note: Alaska's SEA nonstop last flies Oct 2 — two weeks before you'd go. Connect via SLC or DEN.

topSites: Grand Teton NP (Jenny Lake, Cascade Canyon)
Elk rut viewing, National Elk Refuge
locations.verdict: Best scenery & national park access, coldest, pricier from NYC

locations.name: Montana
locations.subtitle: Glacier National Park / Whitefish / Flathead Valley

weather.precip: 1.1 in of snow is the October normal in the valley
weather.notes: November jumps to 8 in. Valley roads stay bare; the mountain roads are where the risk is.

nyc.note: Both NYC nonstops are summer-only and finished in September. Connect via Denver, Chicago or Minneapolis — about 7h50 door to door at best.

sf.note: United's SFO–FCA nonstop runs May 21 through Oct 24, one flight a day, so Oct 16-19 clears it by five days. Earlier reporting had this route dying around Columbus Day; the published range says otherwise.

seattle.note: Alaska year-round, 1h25, roughly 106 flights a month. Much the easiest origin.

topSites: Avalanche Lake and the Trail of the Cedars
Lake McDonald — and the golden eagle migration overhead
Middle Fork of the Flathead, floating and fishing into November
Western larch turning gold across the valley
Many Glacier — Grinnell Lake, Redrock Falls, Apikuni Falls
Whitefish town: breweries, distillery, and a real main street
National Bison Range, Red Sleep Mountain Drive (through Oct 31)
locations.verdict: Cheapest week of the year to be here and you'll have it nearly to yourself — but Logan Pass very likely closes on or before your dates, and every in-park lodge and guided outfitter has already shut.

locations.name: North Carolina
locations.subtitle: Asheville / Blue Ridge Mountains

weather.notes: Warmest by far, peak foliage, humid

nyc.note: Nonstop into AVL from LGA (Delta/American) and EWR (United/Allegiant), both still flying in October. ~2h.

sf.note: No Bay Area nonstop to AVL. Cheaper play: SFO→CLT nonstop on American, then the 2h drive.

seattle.note: No nonstop to AVL. SEA→CLT nonstop on American plus the 2h drive is the sane routing.

locations.verdict: Warmest, easiest & cheapest logistics; fly into CLT and drive ~2hrs

locations.name: Bozeman, MT
locations.subtitle: Big Sky / Paradise Valley / Yellowstone north gate

weather.notes: About a 1-in-6 chance of frozen precipitation on any given day. October averages 4.5in of snow; valley accumulation is possible but unlikely — snow and ice on the passes is the real risk.

nyc.note: United's Newark nonstop runs daily May 21 through Oct 24 — your dates fit with a week to spare. The JFK nonstops (JetBlue, Delta) ended Sept 8 and Sept 5; LGA (American) ended Sept 5.

sf.note: United flies SFO–BZN year-round, daily. Alaska's seasonal SFO run ended Aug 18. No OAK or SJC service.

seattle.note: Alaska and Delta, both year-round and daily — the easiest origin on the whole list.

topSites: Fly fishing the Gallatin, Madison & Yellowstone rivers
Hyalite Canyon hikes and the reservoir
Yellowstone north gate day trip (Gardiner → Lamar Valley)
Bozeman Main Street brewery & distillery crawl
Big Sky / Lone Peak scenic drive up the Gallatin Canyon
Chico Hot Springs soak in Paradise Valley
Museum of the Rockies (the T. rex is genuinely worth it)
locations.verdict: The other Montana, and the easier one to reach — two year-round West Coast nonstops and better fishing. You just trade Glacier for Yellowstone's back door.

booked.title: Pool / Hot Tub / Sauna / Gym | King Bed | Quarry
booked.beds: 7 beds, including two kings and bunk beds
booked.caveat: It's a 3-bedroom, not the 4+ we were searching for — getting to 10 depends on the bunks, so check the bed list against the final headcount.

housing.intro: Whitefish is decided. It's 19 minutes from the airport, 39 from the park entrance, and the only town in the valley with a real main street — which matters more than usual on this trip, because nothing inside the park is open for food and the ski mountain hasn't woken up yet. Mid-October is a genuine dead zone here: Whitefish Mountain closed Sept 20 and doesn't reopen until Dec 4, and park visitation drops to 18% of its July peak. That's why it's cheap, and also why you should check that your restaurant is open before you drive to it. The four other towns are still below for the record — and because a cabin in Columbia Falls is genuinely cheaper if the Whitefish inventory dries up.

areas.name: Whitefish
areas.drive: 19 min to FCA, 39 to the park
areas.vibe: The one town with restaurants, bars and a walkable centre. Most expensive of the five, and the only one that charges resort tax — but the premium is inventory, not tax.
areas.quality: Good — eight 4-5BR properties with published floor rates ($243-389), plus market ADR. Floor rates may not be the October rate.

areas.name: Columbia Falls
areas.drive: 17 min from Whitefish, 20 to the park
areas.vibe: The best-value large-group inventory in the valley and the closest real town to the West Glacier gate. Less to do at night, which matters less than you'd think in a week when nothing's open anyway.
areas.quality: Good — five 4-5BR properties with published floor rates ($216-534) plus two Vacasa homes at $377-579.

areas.name: Kalispell
areas.drive: 24 min from Whitefish, 45 to the park
areas.vibe: Cheapest beds and where the Costco is. Least charming of the five and furthest from the park, but if the group's priority is the number at the bottom of the calculator, it's here.
areas.quality: Weak — exactly one 4BR with a published rate ($366). No local manager publishes rates; one analytics source returned Great Falls data by mistake.

areas.name: West Glacier / Coram
areas.vibe: Wake up at the entrance. The catch is that this corridor is built for summer — the one resort with published rates ends its season Oct 15, the day before you'd arrive, and there's almost no bookable 4BR inventory.
areas.quality: Thin — one 3BR resort ($450 off-season) whose rate calendar stops Oct 15, plus an area-level average. Verify anything here is even open.

areas.name: Bigfork
areas.drive: 38 min from FCA, 55 to the park
areas.vibe: Flathead Lake, an arts-town main street, and a working theatre — the only one of the five with an actual evening option in October. Furthest from Glacier, closest to a rainy-day plan.
areas.quality: Weak — around ten large lakefront homes exist but every price sits behind a booking widget. Largest with a published rate is a 3BR at $434.

notes: Mid-October is a true shoulder trough: Whitefish Mountain closed Sept 20 and reopens Dec 4, and Glacier's October visitation is 18% of its July peak — an 82% drop.
The one published seasonal table in the valley (Great Northern, Coram) shows off-season at 36-39% below peak. Expect a real rate discount nearer 35% than the 80% the occupancy collapse might suggest.

Montana charges 8% lodging tax statewide. Whitefish adds a 3% resort tax (11% total); Columbia Falls, Kalispell, Bigfork and West Glacier add nothing. On a 4-night stay that gap is about $60 — do not pick a town over it.
Cleaning runs $325+ per turnover for a 4BR in this market, and that's the cleaner's price to the host, so the guest-facing fee is usually higher. On four nights it's still the single biggest add-on.
Book by phone. Vacay Whitefish (406-609-9595) has the deepest published 4-5BR inventory in both Whitefish and Columbia Falls; Stay Montana (888-871-7856) holds the big Bigfork lakefront homes.
Anything sleeping 10 usually means 4-5 bedrooms, and Airbnb's guest count includes sofa beds — read the actual bed list.
housing.sourceNote: No public source publishes rates for Oct 15-19, 2026 anywhere in this valley — every booking engine is JavaScript-gated or blocks automated requests. The bands below are published floor rates, operator rate calendars and market averages read Aug 2026. Each area is labelled with how good its data actually is.

costs.foodNote: Montana has no general sales tax. Whitefish's 3% resort tax hits restaurant meals and alcohol but exempts groceries — so cooking in is taxed at zero. Kalispell, Columbia Falls and Bigfork charge nothing on meals either. Costco moved: it's now 345 Cascade Loop, Kalispell, about 17 minutes from Whitefish. Watch for 20% auto-gratuity on parties of six or more at the upscale places, and confirm hours before you drive.

flights.headline: Seattle and SF get nonstops. NYC connects.

rows.detail: Year-round, 1h25, roughly 106 flights a month. Comfortably the easiest origin.
Both NYC nonstops are seasonal and end in September. October is connecting-only, usually via Denver, Chicago or Minneapolis — about 7h50 door to door at best.
Has never had a nonstop in any season.

Alive for your dates: United runs it daily from May 21 to Oct 24, one flight a day, which leaves five days of margin after you fly home. It is still the last week of the season, so a schedule change would hit this before anything else.
No service. Allegiant dropped Oakland entirely. The Bay Area crew flies SFO, or considers Missoula.

flights.caveat: Glacier Park International is a heavily seasonal airport and its own website is stale — it still advertises Allegiant Oakland service that no longer exists. The SFO nonstop clears your dates by five days, but it is the last week of the season, so a schedule trim would hit it before anything else. Missoula is the hedge if that happens, or if FCA fares spike. Spokane is cheaper still but nearly 5 hours away — not worth it for three nights.

alt.title: The Missoula alternative (MSO)
alt.intro: Missoula is the second way into the Flathead: 137 miles south of Whitefish, about 2h45 up US-93 along the east shore of Flathead Lake, and not a mountain pass the whole way. It is a bigger, less seasonal airport than Kalispell, and on US DOT Q1 2026 fare data FCA averages about 18% above it. The trade is the drive — two of them, on arrival and departure days.

rows.detail: Roughly 105 flights a month, 27 departures a week. Seattle already has a year-round nonstop into Kalispell, so this one is only worth it on price.

Daily, and flying in October — but Missoula's own airport lists it as seasonal and no end date is published. United's other Montana seasonal routes stop Oct 24, so assume the same and check before you count on it.

No nonstop from any New York airport, in any season. The NYC three connect via Denver, Chicago, Minneapolis or Salt Lake — the same shape of day as flying into Kalispell, so Missoula buys them nothing but a cheaper fare and a 2h45 drive.

alt.verdict: Worth pricing for the Bay Area two and the Seattle one if FCA fares spike; not worth it for the NYC three, who connect either way and would land on top of a long drive. Renting in Missoula also means returning the cars there — build the drive into both the arrival and the departure day.

plan.title: Four nights in Whitefish
plan.intro: Three days, and they're shaped around one hard hike. Friday is arrival, groceries and a short walk; Saturday is the big one — Apgar Lookout, 7.2 miles and 1,800 feet, deliberately chosen because it sits below every gate NPS might close; Sunday is a guided float on the Middle Fork, which is both the README's 'learn to fish' and the only thing your legs will tolerate the day after the lookout. Assume Logan Pass is shut — NPS targets the third Monday of October, which is your checkout day, and in 2025 it actually closed on Oct 14. Every in-park lodge and restaurant shut in September. What's left is genuinely good: the lower west side is open and empty, the larch are turning, golden eagles are migrating over Lake McDonald, and the Middle Fork fishes into November.
facts: The Quarry Airbnb, Whitefish — picked. 4 nights, in Thu 10/15, out Mon 10/19
Apgar Lookout, Saturday — 7.2 miles round trip, 1,800 ft
54°F day, 29°F night. 1.1in of snow is the October normal in the valley
Sunrise ~8:00, dark by ~6:45. Daylight is the constraint on Saturday, not the miles
Assume the alpine section is closed. Text GNPROADS to 333111 for live status
$35 per vehicle, 7 days. No vehicle reservations required in 2026
Brokeback Mountain — shot an hour north over the Alberta line
Nothing in the park is open for food. Bring lunch every day
bookAhead: Middle Fork float for Sunday — book it now. Great Northern Resort (800-735-7897) at $650 a full day, or Wild River Adventures. Two anglers per boat, so eight people is four boats.
Montana fishing licences at ols.fwp.mt.gov — about $32 each. Needed for the Middle Fork even though fishing inside the park isn't licensed.
The cabin — picked: the Quarry house in Whitefish on Airbnb, Thu 10/15 to Mon 10/19. Lock it in before the rate moves.
Two AWD SUVs at FCA. Seven agencies are in the terminal, and October is the quiet end of the year. Two vehicles is what lets Saturday's group split in half.
Text GNPROADS to 333111 before you leave — it's the live road-status line. Saturday's hike doesn't depend on it; the easy group's afternoon does.
Restaurant reservations, and confirm hours first — you're arriving in the gap between summer and ski season and things close without warning.
plan.caveat: Everything with a price, a distance or a date was verified against NPS, the operator's own site, or published fare and rate data in Aug 2026. Road status is the one thing nobody can verify in advance — it turns on the weather in the week you travel, which is exactly why Saturday's hike was picked below the closure.

days.headline: Land, provision, stretch your legs. Keep it short — tomorrow is 1,800 feet.

blocks.what: Land at FCA, collect two AWD SUVs
blocks.detail: Glacier Park International is 19 minutes from Whitefish — far and away the easiest arrival of anywhere you considered. Seven rental agencies sit right by baggage claim. Take two vehicles even if eight of you would squeeze into one: tomorrow the group splits.

blocks.what: Text GNPROADS to 333111
blocks.detail: Live Going-to-the-Sun Road status. Saturday's hike is below the west entrance and doesn't care what the answer is — but whether Avalanche Lake is reachable does, and so does Sunday.

blocks.what: Costco, 345 Cascade Loop, Kalispell
blocks.detail: Note the address — the old US-93 warehouse closed in Nov 2025 and this is the new one, about 17 minutes from Whitefish. Nothing inside the park sells food in October, so you're packing lunches. Buy tomorrow's on the way in and make them tonight. Groceries are untaxed even in Whitefish.

blocks.what: Check in, then something short on the Whitefish Trail
blocks.detail: The Lion Mountain trailhead is five minutes out of town and the loop there runs about three flat miles through larch — enough to shake out the flight without spending tomorrow's legs. Whitefish City Beach is the lazier version: walk down, look at the lake, walk back.

blocks.what: Walk out into town
blocks.detail: Whitefish is the only town in the valley with a real main street, which is the whole argument for staying here. Craggy Range does burgers at $13.50-18.50; Tupelo Grille is the upscale end at $34-57 — but it auto-applies 20% gratuity to parties of six or more and won't split a bill more than four ways.

blocks.what: Movie night: Brokeback Mountain — then pack
blocks.detail: Filmed just over the Alberta line, an hour or so north of where you're sitting. Old Boy and Internal Affairs are better films and belong to a different trip. Fill water bottles and load packs before anyone opens a second beer; you want to be in the trucks by 7:30.

days.headline: Apgar Lookout, then the lake. The whole day sits below the gate, so no road closure can cancel it.

blocks.what: Out of the house
blocks.detail: Sunrise is around 8:00 in mid-October and it's dark by 6:45, so daylight is the real constraint today — not the mileage. Whitefish to the West Glacier gate is 39 minutes; the Apgar Lookout trailhead is a couple of miles past it down a gravel spur.

blocks.what: Entrance fee
blocks.detail: $35 per vehicle for seven days, so $70 for two. No vehicle reservation is needed in 2026 — that system is gone, replaced by timed parking at Logan Pass you won't reach anyway. The fee drops to $25 on Nov 1, just after you leave.

blocks.what: Apgar Lookout — 7.2 miles round trip, ~1,800 ft
blocks.detail: Three long switchbacks up a south-facing slope to a fire lookout at about 5,200 feet, staring straight down the length of Lake McDonald into the peaks. It's the right big hike for this weekend for three reasons: it's low enough to stay out of early snow, it faces south so it dries and warms first, and it sits just inside the west entrance — below every point NPS might close the road. The slope burned in 2003, so it's open the whole way up: you get the view for the entire climb instead of a tunnel of trees. Budget 4-5 hours with lunch at the top.

blocks.what: Not everyone wants 1,800 feet — plan for that
blocks.detail: With eight to ten people this is never one pace. Whoever taps out takes the second SUV 10 miles up the road to Trail of the Cedars — a 0.7-mile accessible boardwalk loop — and on to Avalanche Lake, 2.3 miles each way for 500 feet. Both groups meet at Lake McDonald Lodge in the afternoon. That is the reason for two vehicles.

blocks.when: If the gate has moved down
blocks.what: Johns Lake Loop and Rocky Point instead
blocks.detail: Avalanche sits above the Lake McDonald Lodge gate, so an early closure puts it out of reach. Johns Lake (3-mile loop, 160 ft) and Rocky Point (1.1 miles, nearly flat) are both below the lodge and stay reachable wherever NPS draws the line. The lookout is unaffected either way.

blocks.what: There is no food in the park
blocks.detail: Every in-park restaurant closed in September — Russell's on Sept 28, Ptarmigan on Sept 21, Two Dog Flats on Sept 13. NPS says the Apgar camp store 'may' be open. Do not count on it. Carry more water than feels necessary: the lookout climb is exposed the whole way and there's nothing on it.

blocks.what: Lake McDonald, and look up
blocks.detail: NPS runs a Hawk Watch from late September through October and roughly 2,000 golden eagles pass Mount Brown in a season — observable from around Lake McDonald Lodge. It's the best-sourced wildlife opportunity of the trip and nobody plans for it. Good place to sit still while the fast group finishes coming down.

blocks.what: Back in Whitefish by 7, and eat properly
blocks.detail: This is the night to have booked something. Tupelo or one of the main-street places — confirm hours when you reserve, because mid-October is when kitchens quietly stop opening on the slow nights.

days.headline: Float the Middle Fork — the one guided thing still running, and the only thing your legs will accept.

blocks.what: Float the Middle Fork — four boats
blocks.detail: This is the README's 'let's all learn to fish', and putting it the day after the lookout is deliberate: you sit down for six hours. Montana's western district season runs to Nov 30, so it's one of the very few guided things still operating in the valley. Great Northern Resort posts $650 for a full day and $490 for a half, two anglers per boat, which means four boats for eight of you.

blocks.what: Licences, and a wrinkle
blocks.detail: The park boundary on the Middle Fork is the high-water mark, so a guided float there does need a Montana licence even though fishing inside the park doesn't. About $32 each at ols.fwp.mt.gov — buy them Friday night, not at the put-in.

blocks.what: National Bison Range, or a slow day in town
blocks.detail: Red Sleep Mountain Drive runs through Oct 31 and is $35 for a van of 10 or more; they ask you to call 406-644-2211 about an hour ahead. Whitefish itself is a fine Sunday — the distillery and the breweries are all on the same walkable street, which is the other half of why you're based here.

blocks.what: Many Glacier
blocks.detail: It's the best of the east side — Grinnell Lake 3.4 miles nearly flat, Redrock Falls 1.8, Apikuni Falls 1 mile for 700 feet. But with Logan Pass shut you go the long way round via US-2 and Marias Pass: 131 miles, about 2h50 each way. Close to six hours in the truck for a day hike, on the day after a 1,800-foot climb. Save it for a June trip.

blocks.what: Something is actually on
blocks.detail: 'The Game's Afoot' runs Oct 16-25 at the Bigfork Center for the Performing Arts — a genuine rainy-day option for eight, and a 40-minute drive. The Vienna Boys Choir is in Kalispell at 7pm, which may or may not be the vibe.

blocks.what: Pack — Monday is a 19-minute departure
blocks.detail: Checkout is Monday 10/19 and FCA is 19 minutes from the house, so leave an hour and you're comfortable; there's no dawn scramble. Monday is also NPS's stated target for shutting the alpine road, so if it's open when you drive out you're watching the last hours of the season. Two things you're just missing: the larch peak Oct 20-31, Kintla and Bowman closer to Oct 22-25, so you catch maybe 60-85% of it — and Bigfork's larch festival, which was Oct 10.

flightStops.note: Nonstop status and last-day dates come from the airports' own published 2026 summer schedules (Jackson Hole, dated Feb 11 2026; Bozeman, Feb 13 2026) and route databases for Kalispell, Asheville and Burlington, all read Aug 31 2026. United's seasonal Montana and Wyoming flying ends Oct 24 across the board — five days after you fly home — so every one of those nonstops is a late-season booking. Schedules can still move; confirm with the airline.
